attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Label-sensitive extraction gap: a small arbitrary circuit for the single function x -> <tau_L,a_N^sim(x)> need not reveal a small quotient-incidence sketch, and high quotient rank alone does not preclude the SAT-labelled linear functional from being simple.
steps: Write the XOR carrier as the F_2 inner product of the SAT truth vector tau_L with the generated incidence vector a_N(x).
Prove the polylog substitution upper bound: SAT circuits of size n^c yield H_N circuits of size N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}.
Try to certify C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} from high rank or expansion of the incidence map x -> a_N(x).
Normalize by quotienting formula space under SAT-preserving symmetries and by cancelling even multiplicities.
Observe that a piecewise affine quotient sketch of cost below N^{1+epsilon} directly computes H_N after hardwiring basis parities and patching sparse exceptions.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The quotient-sketch lemma gives valid upper-bound falsifiers and preserves the target bridge, but it is not a lower-bound method. Promoting it would require a nonrelativizing, real-SAT-specific extraction theorem from small H_N circuits to small quotient sketches, or a direct unrestricted circuit lower bound for H_N.

assumptions: epsilon>0 is fixed; q,rho,d are fixed constants with max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
G_N is target-clean: its circuit description does not contain SAT truth-table advice, although upper-bound falsifiers may hardwire finitely many parity constants.
sim_N is exact SAT-preserving: phi sim_N psi implies SAT(phi)=SAT(psi).
Exceptional seeds are patched by equality circuits of O(N) size per seed.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=xor_{j<=m} SAT(phi_{N,j}(x)), a Boolean function on N-bit seeds, measured in unrestricted nonuniform SIZE.
target object: SAT on L-bit formula encodings, with target consequence SAT notin P/poly and hence NP not subset P/poly if the bridge source lower bound is valid.
controlled interface: a SAT-free generator G_N of size N^rho emits m=ceil(N^q) formulas of length L=(log N)^d, and the carrier consumes their SAT labels only through F_2 parity.
target-preserving condition: L=(log N)^d, d>1, max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, and the claimed source lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} holds for infinitely many N without SAT-label advice in G_N.
quotient incidence: for a SAT-preserving equivalence relation sim_N on L-bit formulas, a_N^sim(x)_C is the parity of generated formulas in class C.

quotient sketch: QSk_{sim,N}(E) is the minimum total circuit cost of a piecewise affine representation of a_N^sim(x), correct outside E exceptional seeds, with SAT parities of affine basis vectors hardwired nonuniformly.

equations.label: xor_incidence_identity
equations.valid_when: Valid when G_N outputs syntactic formula encodings and repeated formulas are counted with parity over F_2.

equations.label: polylog_substitution_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after SAT has n^c-size circuits and the generator has N^rho-size circuits with m=N^q polylog-length queries.

equations.label: target_magnification_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid for infinitely many N against every fixed target exponent c because L=(log N)^d makes L^c=N^{o(1)}.

equations.label: sat_preserving_quotient_identity
equations.valid_when: Requires the equivalence relation to preserve SAT labels on every quotient class used by the generated formulas.

equations.label: quotient_sketch_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Requires a piecewise affine sketch of the quotient incidence vector correct outside E named seeds and allows nonuniform hardwiring of the resulting SAT parities.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a SAT-preserving quotient sim_N and E<N^{epsilon-o(1)} with QSk_{sim,N}(E)<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}. That is a valid falsifier for the source lower bound, not evidence about P vs NP.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a repaired bridge lemma plus a source-audit gate. It proves the target transfer and names an explicit family of upper-bound falsifiers for the barely-superlinear source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a polylog-query XOR generated-SAT carrier, the target bridge remains valid with threshold max{rho,q}<1+epsilon. The source lower bound is credible only after ruling out every SAT-preserving quotient incidence sketch; any subthreshold quotient sketch plus sparse exceptions is a concrete falsifier for C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.

assumptions: The pairing certificate is computable with size N^{rho_pair}.
Every nonresidual pair is SAT-equivalent for the same seed x.
Residual slots are the only slots that can affect the XOR value.
definitions: slot-pairing: a target-clean circuit P_N maps each seed to disjoint slot pairs and residual slots.

SAT-preserving symmetry: each paired formula pair is related by equality, variable renaming, clause permutation, padding by tautological clauses, or another certified transformation preserving satisfiability.
residual exponent: u is such that the number of unpaired or uncertified slots is at most N^u.

equations.label: pair_cancellation
equations.valid_when: Valid when every cancelled pair is certified SAT-equivalent on the same seed before taking the F_2 parity.

equations.label: empty_residual_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when all nonexceptional seeds have complete certified pair cancellation and exceptional seeds are patched nonuniformly.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a generator has high raw range but a subthreshold symmetry-pairing certificate, quarantine the generator; its apparent entropy is parity-cancelled.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This supplies a cheap falsifier search before attempting any arbitrary-circuit lower bound for the XOR carrier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: XOR carriers must be audited after quotienting by easy SAT-preserving symmetries. If most slots are paired with SAT-equivalent mates, the paired portion contributes zero to H_N, so raw slot count q and raw formula-range entropy overstate the source burden.

assumptions: The duplicated formulas can range over a large target-clean family.
The source model is unrestricted circuits, so a constant carrier has O(1) size.
definitions: duplicated-slot generator: G_N emits (psi_1(x),psi_1(x),...,psi_{m/2}(x),psi_{m/2}(x)).
raw entropy measure: any certificate that counts distinct emitted formulas before F_2 cancellation or SAT-preserving quotienting.
odd quotient support: the support of a_N^sim(x), not the multiset of generated slots.

equations.label: duplicate_zero_carrier
equations.valid_when: Valid when the carrier aggregates labels by XOR, so two identical SAT labels cancel over F_2 for every seed.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Any proposed source proof using unreduced slot entropy fails this witness test unless it first passes to odd quotient incidence.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This refutes a tempting rank-only promotion and justifies the quotient-incidence gate as a necessary normal form.
candidate_lemmas.statement: High unreduced incidence rank or high raw formula entropy is not a valid lower-bound certificate for XOR generated-SAT carriers. Duplicated or SAT-equivalent paired slots can make H_N constant while preserving large raw syntactic variation.

control_decision.reason: The branch produced a sharper falsifier and a valid normal form without weakening the polylog-query magnification threshold.

falsifier: fixed-point-free duplicate, variable-renaming, or clause-permutation pairings cancel most XOR slots before any SAT hardness is used.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: Raw range and slot entropy stay near N^q, but the carrier complexity tracks the residual quotient sketch. When u and the pairing-certificate cost are subthreshold, H_N is easy despite the apparent high-rank generated query family.
held_fixed_controls: max{rho,q}<1+epsilon so the polylog-query target transfer remains valid.
The source model is unrestricted nonuniform SIZE on N-bit seeds.
The equivalence relation is exact SAT preservation by syntactic variable renaming and duplicate equality.
G_N contains no SAT truth-table advice; only upper-bound falsifier circuits may hardwire parity constants.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The XOR route can be artificially inflated by SAT-equivalent paired queries. A concrete cancellation experiment tests whether the current source audit measures the real odd quotient incidence or only raw slot entropy.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: For each N choose q in ((1+epsilon)/2,1+epsilon) and L=(log N)^d with d>1. Let G_N emit M=N^q formulas; most slots are pairs (psi, rename_pi(psi)) under variable renaming, while R=N^u residual slots are high-entropy target-clean formulas. H_N is the XOR of all generated SAT labels.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal quotient-incidence sketch bound proving certified pair cancellation, computing the residual quotient incidence below N^{1+epsilon}, and separating target-clean generator information from nonuniform hardwired parity constants.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: residual exponent u, equivalently the odd quotient incidence mass after SAT-preserving pair cancellation.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Circuit-to-SQ simulation gap at tolerance tau_k; no uniform, target-preserving map from SIZE(m^k) deciders to few SQ queries is known.
steps: Compute chi_i=dD_i/dD_0-1 for the source family and certify pairwise correlation <=gamma.
Invoke statistical dimension to rule out SQ(q,tau) distinguishers below q=Theta(1/(gamma+tau^2)).
Try to convert a size m^k circuit for L_m into an SQ algorithm by estimating its acceptance correlations under D_0 and D_i.
The conversion has no valid generic form: an arbitrary circuit may use pointwise structure or advice invisible to bounded expectation queries.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation separates a restricted algorithmic model, not P or P/poly. It becomes relevant to P-vs-NP only after a nonstandard simulator and distributional transfer are proved.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: SQ-Dimension Target Gate

assumptions: All D_i are absolutely continuous with respect to D_0 and queries are bounded in [-1,1].
Pairwise correlations of likelihood ratios are at most gamma except on the diagonal.
The SQ lower bound is distributional and black-box; it is relativizing in spirit and not a circuit lower bound by itself.
Any claimed P-vs-NP use must supply Sim plus a worst-case-to-distributional transfer preserving m,k,eps,tau.
definitions: source object: distributional slice L_m with null D_0 and alternatives {D_i}_{i<=M}, density ratios chi_i=dD_i/dD_0-1, and explicit samplers/evaluators.
target object: SQ(q,tau) distinguishers; audited transfer target is SIZE(m^k) or P algorithms on the same m-bit slice.
controlled interface: Sim_{k,m} maps every size m^k circuit deciding L_m with advantage eps into q<=Q_k(m) SQ queries of tolerance tau_k and comparable advantage.
target-preserving condition: the SAT reduction fixes the distributional slice and labels; the statistic cannot be supplied by padding, advice, or an easy tagged branch.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Parity concepts under the uniform distribution are an immediate falsifier if the route infers circuit hardness from SQ dimension alone.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Converts SQ-hardness enthusiasm into a route-specific bridge with a named missing simulator and quantitative threshold.
candidate_lemmas.statement: SQ dimension gives a valid lower bound only for SQ(q,tau) algorithms. Transfer to SIZE(m^k) requires an explicit circuit-to-SQ simulator on the same distribution; without it, high dimension is not a P-vs-NP route.

dependency_updates.description: Statistical dimension is accepted as a valid lower-bound method only for SQ(q,tau) targets with explicit gamma and tau.
Needed before SQ hardness can affect SIZE(m^k), P/poly, or P-vs-NP proof obligations.
Tagged SAT/parity carriers preserve NP-completeness while destroying target-preservation of the statistic.

falsifiers: Parity concepts give SQ dimension 2^r under the uniform distribution yet have linear-size XOR circuits; this is the core falsifier.
Noisy or labeled parity is SQ-hard at inverse-polynomial tolerance but learnable by Gaussian elimination from samples, falsifying SQ-hard implies P-hard.
A tagged language L(b,x,z)=SAT(x) for b=0 and PARITY(z) for b=1 preserves NP-completeness but lets the SQ statistic live on an easy branch.
A nonuniform circuit can hardwire the planted index i in a distributional family; SQ search hardness need not imply fixed-language circuit hardness.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation does not rule out a genuinely symbolic, non-list proof that quantifies over all circuits of size <=2^{q m}.
steps: Set N=2^m and R=2^{rho m}. Build a constant-weight code of 4R-subsets of [N] with pairwise symmetric difference greater than 2R by greedy packing in the Johnson space.
For each support A in the code, the indicator 1_A has an unrestricted DNF/equality-test circuit of size O(Rm). If rho<q, this is below 2^{q m} for large m.
Because packed tables are pairwise farther than 2R, a single radius-R ball around any listed center can cover at most one packed table.
The greedy packing has log_2 size Omega(R log(N/R)), hence any challenge list covering all these easy tables needs 2^{Omega(m2^{rho m})} centers.
An E-rankable list, or any O(m)-certificate naming only 2^{O(m)} challenges, misses a packed easy table. A verifier accepting distance from that list therefore accepts a subthreshold circuit table.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a source-side falsifier for one implementation of the MCSP carrier. It neither constructs a valid hard row nor proves P != NP.

assumptions: Unrestricted Boolean circuit size is the MCSP measure.
The list L_m may be E-rankable or certificate-dependent, but its anti-ball soundness is only list coverage.
The verifier does not additionally prove a symbolic theorem covering every circuit of size <=2^{q m}.
rho and q are constants with 0<rho<q<1.
definitions: source object: low-D MCSP carrier row T in {0,1}^{2^m} with a claimed anti-ball certificate excluding radius R=2^{rho m} around subthreshold circuits.
target object: an E-uniform language obtained by D-multiplexing and kappa-padding, intended to have circuit lower bound exponent delta.
controlled interface: source row hardness C(T)>2^{q m}, q=epsilon-rho, plus E-canonical distinct-image unranking for at most 2^{D m} rows and no advice.
target-preserving condition: q>0, rho<q for the sparse-packing falsifier, kappa and D fixed constants, and all length choices uniform rather than nonuniform selectors.
challenge-list anti-ball certificate: a proof whose only universal lower-bound content is that T is farther than R from every truth table in an explicitly rankable forbidden list L_m.
sparse easy packing: a family of indicators of 4R-subsets of [N] with pairwise Hamming distance greater than 2R and unrestricted circuit size O(Rm).

equations.label: packing_size
equations.valid_when: Valid when constant-weight subsets of size 4R are greedily packed at distance greater than 2R.

equations.label: list_soundness_threshold

equations.label: conditional_transfer_after_real_hard_row

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If an anti-ball source can be reduced to checking distance from an E-size forbidden list, test it against the 4R-sparse packing; acceptance of any missed sparse indicator is a concrete falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Negative bridge audit: it refutes a tempting sparse anti-ball implementation while preserving the conditional carrier-to-E extraction theorem.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Positive-radius anti-ball certificates cannot be mere E-rankable challenge lists. For N=2^m, R=2^{rho m}, and q=epsilon-rho with rho<q, any list L_m of forbidden centers of size below 2^{Omega(m 2^{rho m})} misses an easy sparse truth table T with C(T)=O(Rm)<=2^{q m} and dist(T,L_m)>R. Thus a verifier whose soundness only excludes L_m has an accepted easy row, a route-specific falsifier for the MCSP no-side carrier.

assumptions: Proof length is O(m) or otherwise E-searchable after declared constants.
Verifier time is 2^{O(m)} and has no nonuniform length advice.
Accepted distinct-image entropy is at most Dm.
The proof system is sound for unrestricted circuits, not merely for uniform algorithms or a restricted circuit class.
definitions: symbolic anti-ball proof: a short proof whose soundness quantifies over all circuits of a given size, not over a sampled or listed challenge set.
row soundness: every accepted row is hard, or an existential hard row is converted by canonical distinct-image multiplexing without advice.
E-canonical unranking: the row index and input bit are computable in time 2^{O(m)} uniformly across lengths.

equations.label: symbolic_soundness
equations.valid_when: Valid when the verifier's proof system is sound for all unrestricted circuits of the declared size.

equations.label: row_lower_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid because exact equality to a small circuit would have distance zero, below the anti-ball radius.

equations.label: multiplexed_extraction
equations.valid_when: Requires uniform padding, bounded distinct-image entropy, and an actually hard accepted row at source length m.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If soundness is average-case, challenge-list, restricted-circuit, or advice-dependent, the transfer is invalid for the P-vs-NP target model.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Positive conditional route lemma identifying the exact proof object still missing.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A symbolic anti-ball proof system would be a valid source interface: if an E-verifier accepts (m,i,pi) only when the emitted row T_i satisfies dist(T_i,C)>2^{rho m} for every unrestricted circuit C of size <=2^{q m}, then C(T_i)>2^{q m} and the existing D-multiplexing/kappa-padding transfer gives an E lower bound with exponent delta<q/(kappa(1+D)). The bridge is conditional and route-level only.

assumptions: Use standard pseudorandom-function-based interpretation of the natural proofs obstruction.
q<1 and rho<1 so the union of circuit balls is exponentially tiny inside all truth tables.
The route aims at unrestricted nonuniform circuit lower bounds, not only uniform lower bounds.
definitions: dense anti-ball property: all truth tables farther than R from every subthreshold circuit truth table.
sparse carrier image: at most 2^{D m} accepted rows among 2^{2^m} truth tables.
natural-proof risk: constructivity in time poly(N) together with largeness at threshold 2^{q m}.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed source becomes a polynomial-in-N decidable large property, the natural-proofs falsifier applies unless a non-natural feature is explicitly proved.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier classifier: it distinguishes the non-large sparse route from invalid dense constructive repairs.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The dense property of being outside all radius-R balls around circuits of size <=2^{q m} is large for q,rho<1 and is decidable in poly(N) only by a natural-proof-like construction. The low-D carrier remains non-large, but any repair that recognizes a dense outside-union set in E should be quarantined under the natural proofs barrier, unless it is demonstrably non-natural or relies on nonconstructive soundness outside the barrier's scope.

falsifiers: challenge-list anti-ball certificate: any E-size list of forbidden centers at positive radius rho<q misses sparse easy packed indicators.

threshold-collapse falsifier: if q=epsilon-rho<=0 then the extracted exponent delta is nonpositive, and if rho>=q the present sparse-packing audit no longer certifies list failure at the claimed threshold.
natural-proofs falsifier: replacing the sparse carrier by the dense outside-union anti-ball property makes the property large and constructively dangerous.
restricted-model falsifier: excluding only uniform algorithms, formulas, AC0, or algebraic circuits does not certify unrestricted MCSP row hardness.
nonuniform-leakage falsifier: length advice, a nonuniform hard-row selector, or a subthreshold interval decoder invalidates the E target transfer.
average-soundness falsifier: a proof that most accepted rows are hard is insufficient unless multiplexing canonically isolates an actual hard distinct image.
